page: Amazon Web Services r9gd.medium is an entry-level memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated 64-bit ARM processor manufactured by AWS, operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 1 physical core and 1 vCPU with 1 thread per core. It is paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio tailored for memory-bound tasks. The instance does not include GPU hardware accelerators.

Storage on the r9gd.medium consists of 59 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage, providing fast read and write access directly on the host rather than relying purely on remote network block devices. Networking is handled via the Nitro platform, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with the instance.

Due to its single-core arm64 design paired with a generous 8.0 GB memory footprint and integrated NVMe capacity, r9gd.medium offers resource density for specialized, low-concurrency operations. However, the single vCPU configuration imposes a hard limit on multithreaded throughput, restricting its viability for parallel computation. Best-fit workloads include standalone in-memory key-value caches, small relational database environments, logging buffers, and development microservices requiring high memory density.
description: Amazon Web Services r9gd.medium is an arm64 memory-optimized virtual machine delivered on the AWS Nitro System. The instance features a single dedicated AWS Graviton core clocked at 3.3 GHz with 1 vCPU and no simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 8.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 gigabyte-to-vCPU ratio designed for memory-intensive entry-level applications. Storage includes 59 GB of bundled high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage, enabling low-latency scratch storage and local caching. Network throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. Without dedicated GPU hardware or multi-core execution capabilities, the instance represents a focused resource profile for workloads requiring elevated memory capacity per core. The server fits deployment scenarios such as lightweight Redis or Memcached nodes, small operational databases, staging environments, and memory-constrained microservices.
